column1: # Guards under scripts/ci/ that run in CI but deliberately NOT in the local
# Docker entry point (scripts/verify-in-docker.sh), and what makes them need
# something a clean container off this repository does not have. Read by
# scripts/ci/check-guard-wiring.py, which fails on any scripts/ci/ guard that is
# neither mirrored into the entry point nor listed here -- so the gap has to be
# decided per guard and cannot silently widen.
# Format: <name>\t<reason>   ("#" starts a comment; a reason is mandatory)
# "Mirror" means the guard's file name appears in a path position in the `gates`
# array, or in a path position in a file the entry point already runs
# (transitively, the same rule as reachability). Three guards are mirrored that
# way without having a gate line of their own: publish-npm.sh,
# local-publish-host.sh and stamp-npm-version.mjs are each named by the harness
# in test-publish-npm.sh, which is mirrored. Of the three the harness really
# exercises publish-npm.sh; local-publish-host.sh runs as far as its
# missing-binary check, and stamp-npm-version.mjs sits behind a --version the
# harness never passes -- so nothing the local entry point runs rewrites the npm
# package.json files, and the tree the run checksums stays as it was.
check-powershell-syntax.py
column2: `--require` needs a real PowerShell to parse scripts/install.ps1; the verify image is Debian bookworm-slim, which has no pwsh in the pocket it installs from, and adding one means the Microsoft package feed. Running the installer is the target-OS leg's job either way.
